subject: ela
cluster: Range of Reading and Level of Text Complexity
intro: Tenth graders read and comprehend literary nonfiction at the high end of the grades 9-10 complexity band, independently and proficiently, applying all skills: central idea, strong evidence, structure, word meaning, author's purpose and rhetoric, and evaluating arguments.

items.prompt:
Read.

The printing revolution spread knowledge and literacy, but it also spread propaganda and deepened conflicts.

What is the central idea?

steps: The passage weighs benefits and harms.
So the central idea is that the printing revolution spread both knowledge and conflict.
solution.answer: The printing revolution spread both knowledge and conflict.

items.prompt:
Read (same passage).

Name one NEGATIVE effect.

steps: So one negative effect was the spread of propaganda.
solution.answer: The spread of propaganda (or deepened conflicts).

items.prompt:
Read.

'Ask not what your country can do for you.'

What rhetorical device gives this line its power?

steps: It reverses the expected phrasing for emphasis.
So the reversal (antithesis/parallelism) gives it memorable emphasis.
solution.answer: A reversal (antithesis), which gives it memorable emphasis.

items.prompt:
Read.

Wetlands filter water and prevent floods but are being drained.

Central idea?

Read.

The author urges stricter limits on pollution.

Purpose?
To support a claim about a text, use the ____ evidence.
